{"rules": ["Model consistently underestimates immediate post-spike volatility; true outcomes often surge 5-10% above forecast within the first 3 days of a rally.", "Forecast exhibits severe mean reversion bias, predicting smooth linear growth while actual data shows sharp peaks followed by rapid declines (volatility clustering).", "Sentiment spikes (0.33) precede price surges but are insufficient to prevent subsequent overcorrection; model fails to weight sentiment as a trigger for high-variance events.", "Model ignores the 'mean reversion' pattern where prices spike above 78-80 and immediately drop back toward 65-70 within 10 days, creating a systematic negative bias in the second half of the forecast horizon.", "Forecast assumes low volatility (tight range ~0.03/day) whereas true outcomes display high dispersion (>4/day), leading to consistent under-prediction of downside risk after rallies."]
